title: Building and leading agile teams
blurb: Apply the four considerations for building agile teams: co-decided values, training plans and the skill matrix, value-based motivation and visual management.
question: Saltmarsh's new service design team is unsure which decisions it can take itself and which must go to the repairs director under the association's rules. Which consideration for building and leading agile teams should be applied?

teach.h: Teams that manage themselves need building
teach.body: Agile teams self-manage within boundaries, and leaders serve them: making sure people are supported and have what they need. That does not happen by announcing it. PRINCE2 Agile names four considerations for building and leading agile teams: co-deciding team values and accountabilities; empowering teams with training plans; motivation through value-based incentives and personal values; and visual management with team dashboards. Exam questions describe a team problem and ask which one applies.

head: Consideration
What it settles
Typical tool
rows: Limits of self-management; when to escalate

teach.body: The team agrees its values and who is accountable for what, together, not by decree. The point is that everyone understands the boundaries of self-management and when decisions must be escalated because of organizational guidelines. Team values and norms are a topic of the project kickoff workshop, where they help create an agile culture of openness and self-management.

teach.h: Training plans and the team skill matrix
teach.body: To support training plans and empower team members, a team skill matrix is often used. It visually represents current and planned future expertise and skills, showing strengths, gaps and areas for development, so the right people take the right tasks and training needs are clear. It is completed collaboratively in the project kickoff workshop and, for delivery teams, shown on the team dashboard. Pair it with a training and coaching plan: theory plus coaching on the job.

teach.caption: Current AND planned skills: it drives the training plan and shows where nobody is strong yet.

teach.h: Motivation: value-based incentives and personal values
teach.body: Wide adoption of the agile mindset is critical, so people need motivating to adopt agile values. One technique: peers assess each other and award points or a fictional currency for behaviour that models agile values. Because most people need tangible incentives alongside intangible ones such as purpose and recognition, balance this with personal values. Team values can also be used in peer-based assessment, often in team retrospectives. Incentives on their own cannot guarantee change lasts.

teach.caption: Use them together; a bonus scheme by itself is the classic wrong answer.

teach.h: Worked scenario: Saltmarsh service design team (AS6)
teach.body: Saltmarsh's service design team of six comes from the contact centre, repairs and tenant engagement, uses Kanban in two-week iterations and is led by Raj Malhotra. In the kickoff workshop the team co-decides its values and agrees which changes must go to the repairs director. It builds a skill matrix showing nobody can run tenant research with older tenants, so two members are trained and coached. Peers award points for collaboration, balanced with recognition at demos. The team designs its own dashboard.

teach.text: Classic traps: team dashboards are CO-CREATED by each team, not designed by the project manager and handed over. A skill matrix shows skills, not decision rights (that is the delegation matrix). Points or bonuses must be balanced with intangible motivators and personal values. And co-decided values do not mean the team decides everything: they make clear when to escalate.

items: Four considerations (4.5): values and accountabilities, training plans, value-based motivation, visual management.
Co-decided values and accountabilities set the limits of self-management and when to escalate.
The team skill matrix shows current and planned skills and supports training plans.
Peer-awarded points for agile behaviour, balanced with purpose, recognition and personal values.
Team values can drive peer-based assessment in retrospectives.
Team dashboards give visual management; each team co-creates its own.

summary: You can now match a team problem in a scenario to the right consideration for building and leading agile teams, and apply it: co-decided values and accountabilities, training plans with a skill matrix, balanced value-based motivation and visual management with team-created dashboards.

A.q: Saltmarsh's service design team, drawn from three departments, keeps stopping work to ask whether it may change a contact centre script itself or must refer it to the repairs director under the association's rules. Which consideration for building and leading agile teams should be applied?
options: Empowering teams with training plans
Co-deciding team values and accountabilities
Motivation through value-based incentives
Visual management with team dashboards
A.why: Co-deciding team values and accountabilities makes clear the boundaries of self-management and when decisions must be escalated because of organizational guidelines (4.5).

whyNot.0: Training plans and the skill matrix address skill gaps, not decision limits.
whyNot.2: Value-based incentives address motivation to adopt agile values.
whyNot.3: Team dashboards make information visible; they do not settle when to escalate.

A.q: Pinewick's store operations team must set up collection lockers, but nobody on the team has done it before and two members want to learn. The project manager wants a visual view of current and planned skills to support a training plan. What should the team use?
options: A delegation matrix of decision areas
A list of agreed team values and norms
A cumulative flow diagram of the work
A team skill matrix built with the team
A.why: To support training plans and empower members, a team skill matrix visually represents current and planned future expertise and skills (4.5, 7.4.1).

whyNot.0: A delegation matrix shows who decides what, not skills.
whyNot.1: Team values and norms set expectations of behaviour, not skill levels.
whyNot.2: A cumulative flow diagram shows work in each workflow state and bottlenecks.

A.q: At Draycott, maintenance engineers in the trial cannot see what the software team is working on or what is blocked. The project manager wants better visual management for the team. Which action BEST applies PRINCE2 Agile guidance?
options: The software team co-creates its own team dashboard
The project manager designs a dashboard for the team
The team emails a weekly written checkpoint report
The board updates the project dashboard each week
A.why: Visual management with team dashboards is a 4.5 consideration, and team dashboards are co-created by each team, not dictated (Table 13.8).

whyNot.1: A dashboard dictated by the project manager goes against team ownership and self-management.
whyNot.2: A weekly written report is less visible and timely than a dashboard the team keeps current.
whyNot.3: The board pulls information from the project dashboard; it does not maintain it, and that dashboard is project level.

B.q: Callowmere's web team wants more people to model agile values. The team agrees that colleagues may award each other points for behaviour such as openly sharing problems, and pairs this with recognition at demos and a conversation about each person's own values. Which consideration is being applied?
options: Co-deciding team values and accountabilities
Empowering teams with training plans
Motivation through value-based incentives
Visual management with team dashboards
B.why: Peer-awarded points for model agile behaviour, balanced with intangible motivators and personal values, is motivation through value-based incentives and personal values (4.5).

whyNot.0: Co-deciding values sets boundaries and escalation, not a reward scheme.
whyNot.1: Training plans address skills, supported by the skill matrix.
whyNot.3: Dashboards make work visible; they are not an incentive scheme.

B.q: At Easterholm, the digital team wants to use its agreed team values to assess, peer to peer, how well members worked together during the sprint that has just ended. In which workshop is this MOST typically done?
options: The team retrospective workshop
The team planning workshop
The progress review workshop
The agile enablement workshop
B.why: Team values can be used in peer-based assessments, often as part of team retrospectives, where the team reviews processes and teamwork for the past iteration (4.5).

whyNot.1: Team planning prepares the next iteration: backlog refinement, estimation and iteration planning.
whyNot.2: The progress review assesses project status and demos products to stakeholders.
whyNot.3: The agile enablement workshop reviews Agilometer results and agile-adoption risks with the board.

B.q: Larkspur's data team has just been formed for the Fair Fares project. The project manager wants members to map their skills together, find gaps and overlaps, and put the result on their team dashboard. In which workshop should this be done?
options: The project initiation workshop
The project kickoff workshop
The team planning workshop
The release planning workshop
B.why: The team skill matrix is a topic of the project kickoff workshop, completed collaboratively to map skills and identify gaps or overlaps (Table 13.8, 7.4.1).

whyNot.0: The project initiation workshop covers the Agilometer, management approaches, project DoR and DoD, personas and the release map.
whyNot.2: Team planning prepares an iteration's work, not the team's skill map.
whyNot.3: Release planning updates the release map at stage boundaries.

C.q: At Saltmarsh, the project manager designs a dashboard layout with fixed metrics and asks the service design team to use it from the next iteration, so that every team reports the same way. Is this an appropriate application of visual management, and why?
options: Yes, because consistent layouts help the project manager pull data
Yes, because visual management with dashboards is a key consideration
No, because team dashboards should be co-created by each team
No, because the team dashboard replaces the project's highlight report
C.why: Visual management with team dashboards is a 4.5 consideration, but team dashboards are co-created by each team, not dictated (Table 13.8). Imposing one undermines ownership and self-management.

whyNot.0: Easier data gathering does not justify dictating the team's own dashboard.
whyNot.1: True that visual management matters, but the verdict is wrong because the dashboard is imposed.
whyNot.3: The team dashboard replaces the checkpoint report; the project dashboard replaces the highlight report.

C.q: To encourage Draycott's engineers to adopt agile values, the operations director introduces peer-awarded points for collaborative behaviour, plus recognition at each progress review and team conversations about personal values. Is this an appropriate application of building and leading agile teams, and why?
options: Yes, because it balances tangible incentives with other motivators
Yes, because points make adopting the agile values compulsory
No, because any incentive scheme undermines self-management
No, because motivating staff is the project executive's duty
C.why: Book 4.5 describes peer-assessed points for model agile behaviour, balanced with intangible motivators such as purpose and recognition, and with personal values. This plan does all three.

whyNot.1: Points reward behaviour; they do not and should not make values compulsory.
whyNot.2: PRINCE2 Agile describes value-based incentives as a technique; they need balance, not removal.
whyNot.3: Motivating teams is part of building and leading teams, not a duty reserved to the executive.

C.q: In Larkspur's kickoff workshop, the app team co-decides its team values and agrees that any change to the payment interface beyond the agreed scope must be escalated to the project manager, in line with company rules. Is this an appropriate application of building and leading agile teams, and why?
options: Yes, because the team coach should set the team's values for it
Yes, because the team now knows its limits and when to escalate
No, because a self-managing team should decide all such matters
No, because escalation rules belong in the project canvas instead
C.why: Co-deciding team values and accountabilities means understanding the boundaries of self-management and when decisions must be escalated due to organizational guidelines (4.5).

whyNot.0: Values are co-decided by the team; a coach facilitates rather than sets them.
whyNot.2: Self-management works within boundaries; some decisions must be escalated.
whyNot.3: The project canvas is the business justification, not where team escalation rules sit.

reteach.title: Building a five-a-side team
reteach.question: A new five-a-side football team forms from colleagues in different departments. What do they need to sort out before the season?

blocks.h: Four things a new team sorts out
blocks.body: They agree how they will play and who calls what on the pitch (values and accountabilities, and when to ask the captain). They work out who can play in goal and who needs practice (skill matrix and training). They find what keeps them turning up: a points table for fair play, but also the fun and pride (value-based motivation). And they keep a shared board of fixtures and results everyone can see (team dashboard).

blocks.text: The team makes its own board. A board designed by the manager and handed over is the classic wrong answer.

explain.body: Co-decided by the team so everyone knows the boundaries of self-management and when decisions must be escalated under organizational guidelines. Team values and norms are a kickoff workshop topic.

test.q: Easterholm's digital team is unsure whether it may change the wording of eligibility questions or must refer this to the principal social worker under council rules. What should the team do?
options: Ask the project board to rule on each wording change
Let each developer decide wording changes case by case
Leave the wording as it is until the next stage boundary
Co-decide values and accountabilities, with escalation
test.why: Co-deciding team values and accountabilities clarifies the limits of self-management and when to escalate under organizational guidelines (4.5).

whyNot.0: Sending each change to the board removes self-management and slows the team.
whyNot.1: Deciding case by case without agreed limits risks breaching council rules.
whyNot.2: Waiting for a stage boundary delays the work without resolving the uncertainty.

explain.body: The team skill matrix shows current and planned future skills, supporting training plans and empowering members. Built collaboratively in the kickoff workshop; shown on the team dashboard.

test.q: Callowmere's web team has no one who can test with screen readers, and two members are keen to learn. Which artifact BEST supports a training plan for this?
options: A delegation matrix of the team's decision areas
The project dashboard reviewed by the board
A team skill matrix showing planned skills
The communication management approach
test.why: A team skill matrix visually represents current and planned future expertise, supporting training plans and empowering team members (4.5).

whyNot.0: A delegation matrix shows decision authority, not skills.
whyNot.1: The project dashboard serves the board's view of progress, not team skills.
whyNot.3: The communication management approach covers communication and feedback.

explain.body: Peers award points or a fictional currency for behaviour modelling agile values; balance with intangible motivators (purpose, recognition) and personal values. Team values can be used in peer assessment at retrospectives.

test.q: Pinewick's head of e-commerce plans to reward agile behaviour with a cash bonus decided by managers, and nothing else. Which change would BEST align this with PRINCE2 Agile guidance?
options: Raise the bonus so that it has a stronger effect
Link the bonus to the number of stories delivered
Pay the bonus to the team instead of to individuals
Let peers award points and add recognition and values
test.why: Book 4.5 describes peer-assessed points for model agile behaviour, balanced with intangible motivators and personal values.

whyNot.0: A bigger bonus is still a tangible incentive with no balance.
whyNot.1: Rewarding story counts measures output, not agile values.
whyNot.2: Who receives it changes little; it is still one tangible incentive decided by managers.

explain.body: Team dashboards make information visible to everyone. Each team co-creates its own in the kickoff workshop; the team dashboard replaces the checkpoint report and the project manager pulls information from it.
explain.cite: PRINCE2 Agile V2 book 4.5, Tables 12.1 and 13.8

test.q: At Larkspur, the project manager wants to know each team's progress without asking for written checkpoint reports. Which approach BEST fits PRINCE2 Agile?
options: Pull information from each team's dashboard
Ask each team for a daily written progress email
Attend every team's stand-up without asking first
Have project support draw up a dashboard for each team
test.why: The team dashboard replaces the checkpoint report, and the project manager pulls information from it (Table 12.1); each team co-creates its own (Table 13.8).

whyNot.1: Daily written emails replace one push report with another.
whyNot.2: The project manager attends stand-ups only with the delivery team's agreement (Table 12.1).
whyNot.3: Project support can update and pull from dashboards, but each team's dashboard is co-created by the team.
